standard_prerequisites.use: Propagate K-flatness and the isomorphism c from the algebra through sums of shifts, the split filtration extensions, and the final filtered colimit.

core_obligations: The comparison map and the claim (proof lines 5732-5740): for every differential graded A-module M there is the canonical map c_M : M tensor_R R' to M tensor_A A'; the proof establishes that for property-(P) modules P the map c_P is an isomorphism and P is K-flat as a complex of R-modules, from which the three stated parts follow through the definition of the derived tensor product.

The graded pieces (proof lines 5742-5752): c_A is an isomorphism and A is K-flat by hypothesis; both properties pass to direct sums of shifts of A (more-algebra-lemma-colimit-K-flat for the sums), hence hold for the filtration quotients F_{p+1}P/F_pP.

Induction over the split filtration (proof lines 5753-5764): the short exact sequences 0 to F_pP to F_{p+1}P to the quotient to 0 are split exact as graded modules, so by induction c_{F_pP} is an isomorphism for all p and each F_pP is K-flat (more-algebra-lemma-K-flat-two-out-of-three).
The colimit (proof lines 5765-5780): since P is the filtered colimit of the F_pP, c_P is an isomorphism and P is K-flat by more-algebra-lemma-colimit-K-flat, completing the claim.
proof_roadmap: Set up the canonical comparison map c_M and reduce the lemma to its behaviour on property-(P) modules.
Check both properties on the algebra and propagate them to the filtration quotients.
Induct through the split filtration with the two-out-of-three lemma.
Conclude at the filtered colimit with the colimit K-flatness lemma.
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the derived restriction functor of a K-flat differential graded algebra under base change, its commutation with the ground-ring derived tensor, and the representing module for K-flat inputs (statement lines 5720-5731). The proof (lines 5733-5780) does the real work on property-(P) modules: the canonical comparison map is shown to be an isomorphism with K-flatness simultaneously, by propagating both properties from the algebra through the sums of shifts, the split filtration (two-out-of-three lemma) and the filtered colimit (colimit K-flatness lemma). H2: the simultaneous induction over the property-(P) filtration is the argument; the passage from the claim to the three stated parts is the defining formalism of the derived tensor cited at the start.
